name: cmp
one_line: compare two files byte by byte
plain: `cmp` tells you whether two files are identical, and if not, where the first difference is. It works on any file, including binaries, because it compares bytes, not lines.
It is the right tool to check that a copy, a download or a transfer did not change anything.
when: Verify a copy: cmp original copy && echo identical.
Find the first byte that differs between two binaries or images.

examples.title: Are they identical?
examples.explain: cmp prints nothing and exits with 0 when the files are the same, so && echo runs. If they differ it says where.

examples.title: Where is the first difference?
examples.explain: Prints 'a.bin b.bin differ: byte 17, line 1': the byte offset of the first difference (counted from 1).

examples.title: Show the differing bytes  (-b)
examples.explain: Adds the two differing byte values (and their characters) to the report.

examples.title: List all differences  (-l)
examples.explain: Prints, for every differing byte, its position (decimal) and the two values in octal. Good for seeing exactly what a patch changed.

examples.title: Only the exit status  (-s)
examples.cmd: cmp -s a b && echo same || echo different
examples.explain: -s prints nothing; use it in scripts and read the result with $?.

examples.title: Skip bytes and limit  (-i, -n)
examples.explain: -i 100 skips the first 100 bytes of both files; -n 50 compares at most 50 bytes. Use it to ignore a changing header.

options.plain: Skip the first SKIP bytes of both files; SKIP1:SKIP2 skips a different number in each file.
Output the byte number and the differing byte values for every difference.
Print nothing; only set the exit status.

mistakes: Exit status: 0 identical, 1 different, 2 trouble (for example a missing file).
Byte numbers start at 1 and -l shows values in octal.
For text files diff gives more useful output than cmp.
Comparing files of different length: cmp reports EOF on the shorter file.
try: Copy a file, change one byte with xxd -r, and find it with cmp -l.
Verify that two downloads are identical.
Compare only the data part of two files, skipping a 16-byte header.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
